analyst_view.overall: Milan (4th, 24 pts) host surprise side Frosinone (6th, 20 pts), who have been scoring and shooting a lot lately. Frosinone miss top scorer Raimondo (ankle, out until mid-December), the suspended Bracaglia, and probably Grillitsch and Terzic, all already counted by the numbers. Milan's defence is stretched: Tomori (out since 28 October, back around end of November) and Gabbia are out and Pavlovic is doubtful, while Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze are also out; only Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze are on the numbers' list. Referee Luca Pairetto is one of the strictest in Serie A (4.9 cards per game), which the numbers already add. News for this match was thinner than for others: mostly injury tables and a probable-lineup page, no dedicated preview article.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and already take about 19% off Frosinone for Raimondo and more for Bracaglia and Terzic. Tomori's absence and the doubt over Pavlovic are not on the numbers' list and leave Milan's back line thin (De Winter and Gila expected), so a mild lean higher to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, with Frosinone's high recent corner count already adding about 10% and Milan's low one taking some off. Nothing in the team news changes how either side gets the ball wide, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already raised about a third for Pairetto's strict record (4.9 per game in 31 games). That is already a high figure for Serie A and neither side has a suspension worry or derby edge, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.3 shots, already lifted about 24% on Frosinone's side for their heavy recent shooting (137 in 6). Without Raimondo, whose absence the numbers count only on goals, Frosinone may shoot a little less, while Milan's thin defence could allow more, so these roughly cancel and I stay at 33.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, already lifted for Frosinone's accurate recent shooting. A Milan defence without Tomori and possibly Pavlovic, not on the numbers' list, is a small reason for about 11.1.
